description: Public development cases for package fit, clarification, and capability boundaries, including workforce safety and privacy, resource-efficiency discovery, safe personal decision preparation, clinical-advice boundaries, validated instruments, digital-only coverage, and live adaptive-interview requests. Labels are provisional and are not a validated benchmark or universal quality oracle.

cases.brief: A SaaS team wants to understand recent workarounds and unmet needs before choosing what to build.
A provider says it wants to check account progress, but examples focus on a frustrating support interaction; it is unclear whether the goal is agreed-outcome progress or service friction.
Operations wants to improve a specific handoff between shifts, including information gaps and blockers.
A sponsor is exploring project outcomes, dependencies, and constraints before deciding whether to fund discovery; this is not a funding-eligibility assessment.
A school wants feedback on access and experience in a course, not grades or learner ability. Some respondents are minors.
A clinic wants local feedback on appointment access and communication only, avoiding diagnosis and clinical outcomes.
A person wants a private reflection tool, but the host has not established whether they want practical goal planning or a broader wellbeing reflection.
A hiring team wants candidates' feedback on clarity and access after a completed hiring process, and confirms answers cannot affect selection.
A hiring manager wants applicants to answer a questionnaire so the team can rank and advance candidates.
At day 30, a team wants to identify whether new employees have role clarity, tools, and practical support; responses will not assess performance.
A delivery team and supplier want to review a named milestone against agreed requirements to improve coordination, not make procurement or contract-award decisions.
A safety team wants non-punitive learning about conditions around a past near miss. A separate monitored channel handles active hazards and statutory reporting.
A worker wants to use this questionnaire to report a currently active hazard and expects the host to respond or escalate it.
A team wants to collect evidence gaps and preparation needs ahead of an auditor; it does not ask survee to certify compliance or determine a person's status.
A nonprofit asks for an evaluation of program outcomes but also wants to learn what local residents prioritize; the target decision and respondent group are not clear.
An event organizer wants a live moderated interview guide and promises responses will be anonymous, although survee stores responses under person-linked private links and hosts can view them.

A plant wants a short, person-linked questionnaire about recurring production delays and routine operations-maintenance coordination over the last month. The host will use responses only for team-level process improvements, explains who can see answers, avoids small-group reporting, and directs current hazards and incidents to existing monitored procedures.

After a plant's approved maintenance workflow change has been implemented, operations and maintenance want a short follow-up about adoption barriers and recurring coordination friction. They will use responses for team-level improvement only, not to approve the change, assess hazards, or judge individual workers.

A process-safety owner wants survee to collect hazard-review answers, approve a proposed equipment change, and confirm that the process is cleared for startup under the site's management-of-change procedure.

A home-care provider wants family caregivers to describe access and communication problems in a recent, non-clinical service interaction so the provider can improve its local service. It does not seek a clinical outcome measure or a standardized score.
A hospice provider wants survee to reproduce the CAHPS Hospice Survey for family caregivers, calculate its standardized measures, and compare the results with published benchmarks.

An employer wants an anonymous workforce pulse about workload, stress, and team climate, including small-team breakdowns. The employer requires that responses cannot be linked to individual participants.

A nonprofit wants to administer the CFPB Financial Well-Being Scale in survee, calculate each participant's score, and compare scores before and after financial coaching. The host has not selected another scoring system or privacy method.

A regional health service wants survee to produce a representative estimate of access barriers for every patient, including people with limited internet access, limited English, or assistive-technology needs. The service can distribute only one QR-code questionnaire and will not provide assisted, paper, phone, or other participation routes. It plans to publish the results as representative of the whole patient population.

An industrial maintenance group wants an AI agent to conduct a live conversational interview, invent follow-up probes from each answer, remember each worker’s prior conversations, and follow the same people every month for six months. It requires a responsive interviewer rather than a fixed, self-completed questionnaire.

A food-processing site wants operators to describe recent conditions where energy, water, material use, or waste might be improved, so its qualified energy and operations team can investigate. The host does not want respondents to estimate savings or emissions, authorize changes, or report hazards through this questionnaire. It will preserve a separately monitored safety route and review suggestions without individual performance scoring.

A person wants a short questionnaire to organize their own priorities, known options, questions, and uncertainties before a conversation with a qualified care professional. It must not recommend a treatment or speak for anyone else.
A clinic wants survee to ask about symptoms and personal circumstances, score treatment options, and tell each patient which treatment is best for them.
